evidence.claim: EcoCycle Group describes itself as comprising EcoCycle, EcoBatt, EcoBatt Safety, Eco E-Waste, Recycal, Castings Tasmania and ACL Metal Powders.
evidence.notes: Self-description; ASIC group structure not checked.

evidence.claim: Doug Rowe is publicly described as EcoCycle Group Chief Executive Officer / Managing Director; Nick Dodd as EcoCycle General Manager; Tom Susen as Group Risk and Compliance Manager.
evidence.notes: Trade-press profile quoting the company.

evidence.claim: The group is 'owned by the Rowe family'.
evidence.notes: 2014: Ecocycle assets bought from CMA Recycling receivers and placed under management of Nick Dodd and Doug Rowe; Doug described as owner of Recycal; Recycal described as family-owned. Group-level shareholding needs an ASIC extract (companion report agrees ownership not established).

evidence.claim: EcoCycle publicly contrasts itself with recyclers that wipe and on-sell computers, stating that it physically destroys data-bearing items.
evidence.notes: Supports the destruction-first characterisation for EcoCycle itself.

evidence.claim: Eco E-Waste's secure data disposal page promises physical destruction and says it does not refurbish or resell e-waste.
evidence.notes: Read by the companion 28 Nov report; this pass could not retrieve the page. Consistent with E04. Screenshot with date before quoting verbatim.

evidence.claim: Eco E-Waste is EcoCycle's electronics recycling company with national pick-up coverage, sorting into material streams and robotic removal of mercury-containing parts.
EcoCycle claims AS 5377 certification and was reported in April 2025 as achieving R2v3 certification.
evidence.notes: Certificates, sites and R2v3 scope/appendices (e.g. any test-and-repair scope) not inspected.

evidence.claim: Ecocycle Pty Ltd's FY23/24 NTCRS annual report records 85,333 kg collected against a co-regulatory recycling target of 77,466 kg.
evidence.notes: Published on DCCEEW. Indicates a small NTCRS footprint relative to the scheme.

evidence.claim: Ecocycle is a current approved NTCRS co-regulatory arrangement.
evidence.notes: Prior repo research used the DCCEEW list of 20 May 2026; National EPA now administers the list — re-check before relying on it.

evidence.claim: EcoBatt/EcoCycle opened a battery-in-device shredding (BIDS) plant in Campbellfield (launch reported 3 Sep 2025) with $2 million from Victoria's Circular Economy Infrastructure Fund: Hazardous Waste Round 3, recovering up to 95% of materials at up to 1 t/hour.
evidence.notes: Government release plus industry report.

evidence.claim: A separate April 2024 Victorian announcement awarded $2.5 million to Ecobatt for a lithium battery processing plant in Campbellfield; Sustainability Victoria lists Ecocycle Pty Ltd as project lead.
evidence.notes: Do not merge with the $2m BIDS grant without checking whether they are the same project.

evidence.claim: EcoBatt claims about 7,500 public drop-off points and a company-owned transport fleet.
evidence.notes: Claim reported in trade press; not independently audited.

evidence.claim: Woolworths offers battery and mobile phone recycling units in all supermarkets with Ecobatt; items are collected by EcoCycle, sorted and sent for recycling; customers are told to delete data first.
evidence.notes: Dubbo store-level presence not confirmed by visit.

evidence.claim: In 2021 Woolworths said Ecobatt would split batteries for recycling and send remaining phone components to MobileMuster.
evidence.notes: May have changed since 2021.

evidence.claim: BIG W added household battery and mobile phone recycling units to all 177 stores (from Oct 2022); BIG W's page names EcoBatt/EcoCycle, mentions MobileMuster and prohibits retrieval of deposited devices.
evidence.notes: Store rollout verified in this pass; recycler and no-retrieval terms read by the companion report.

evidence.claim: Coles battery bins are managed by Close the Loop and Ecobatt under B-cycle.
evidence.notes: Batteries only; no phone collection stated.

evidence.claim: Bunnings battery units are serviced by Ecobatt and do not accept products with embedded batteries.

JB Hi-Fi stores have battery and phone collection points (Eco E-Waste names JB bins); JB's booked e-waste service is with Ecoactiv; consumer trade-in is via Assurant; JB Hi-Fi Business ITAD uses a certified partner with Blancco erasure.
evidence.notes: Eco E-Waste bin naming and Assurant trade-in read by the companion report; Dubbo store operator not confirmed.

evidence.claim: The Good Guys accepts small e-waste and batteries in store, has TV e-waste cages at selected stores and runs a trade-in portal; a Dubbo listing names Ecycle Solutions for TVs/computers.
evidence.notes: Dubbo Ecycle Solutions listing read by the companion report; current contract to confirm. EcoBatt battery partnership unconfirmed.

evidence.claim: Ecycle Solutions is a wholly owned QLS Group subsidiary and a separate NTCRS co-regulator, historically collecting via retailer drop-offs including Harvey Norman and The Good Guys.
evidence.notes: Not part of EcoCycle Group. Current Dubbo retail role unconfirmed.

evidence.claim: MobileMuster says collected items are dismantled in Australia and that circuit boards, batteries and plastics are processed by its recycling partner in Singapore.
In 2019 MobileMuster's manager said none of the phones it collects are resold and data is destroyed during disassembly.
evidence.notes: Policy may have changed; re-confirm.

evidence.claim: MobileMuster partners with charities such as The Reconnect Project (reuse) and acts as recycling partner for commercial reuse programs.
evidence.notes: This is the most transferable reuse-partner model found.

evidence.claim: Spyro Kalos was quoted in September 2025 as EcoCycle's National Partnerships Manager for Australia and New Zealand (he was previously MobileMuster's manager).
evidence.notes: Role may have changed; confirm before writing.

evidence.claim: Officeworks Bring it Back says items may be reused or repurposed by charitable organisations where appropriate, or recycled through certified partners; over 11,000 tonnes collected since 2015 including trade-in.
evidence.notes: Reuse share and Dubbo handling unknown.

evidence.claim: Officeworks' trade-in partner Moorup kept 4,753 products in use in 2024; Officeworks also partners with Circonomy.
Dubbo has Officeworks, JB Hi-Fi Home and BIG W/Woolworths (Orana Mall), Harvey Norman (223 Cobra St) and The Good Guys stores.
evidence.notes: Coles, ALDI, Bunnings and telco store presence not checked this session.

evidence.claim: Whylandra accepts household e-waste free, operates under EPL 6058 and participates in the NSW EPA embedded battery trial.
The NSW EPA embedded batteries trial ran from September 2024 to September 2026, Dubbo was among the first 21 CRCs, and NTCRS products such as laptops are excluded and sent to e-waste collection.
evidence.notes: Processor and post-September 2026 status unknown.

evidence.claim: Council small CRC stations at Dubbo and Wellington customer centres and Dubbo library accept mobile phones and accessories, smoke detectors and ink cartridges.
evidence.notes: Downstream collector not named.

evidence.claim: Council's recorded Matthews Metals e-waste arrangement expired 30 June 2025; the current contractor is not publicly verified.
evidence.notes: From prior repository research.

evidence.claim: The NTCRS operates under the Recycling and Waste Reduction Act 2020 and 2021 Rules; the National EPA became its regulator on 1 July 2026.
The PC interim report found the NTCRS focus on recycling results in some functional or repairable products being dismantled or destroyed, and recommended reuse and repair targets (Rec 9.2).
evidence.notes: Recommendation, not law.

evidence.claim: The PC circular economy final report was handed to Government on 22 August 2025, released 16 January 2026 and tabled 23 January 2026.
Ecocycle lodged a final-round submission (No. 217) to the PC inquiry, received 11 April 2025.
evidence.notes: Existence only.

evidence.claim: Ecocycle's submission prioritises NTCRS reform and audit transparency before reuse targets and stresses consumer expectations of destruction.
evidence.notes: Page 3 read by the companion report; not re-read in this pass.

evidence.claim: NSW's Product Lifecycle Responsibility Act 2025 was assented 9 April 2025; the Product Lifecycle Responsibility Regulation 2026 creates a mandatory battery stewardship scheme, with embedded batteries in policy scope.
evidence.notes: Commencement dates for specific obligations not confirmed.

evidence.claim: WorkVentures told the PC that the NTCRS disincentivises device reuse for digital inclusion.
evidence.notes: Stakeholder view.

evidence.claim: ANZRP (TechCollect) told the PC that the NTCRS framework does not recognise or reward product reuse.
evidence.notes: Stakeholder view from a co-regulator.

evidence.claim: Telstra trade-in is managed by Assurant; Vodafone says traded-in devices may be refurbished, resold or recycled; telco stores host MobileMuster bins.
evidence.notes: Trade-in is a reuse stream that bypasses recycling bins.

evidence.claim: EcoCycle has a NSW site at 22 Christie Street, St Marys, under NSW EPL 21136.
evidence.notes: EPL read by the companion report; licence scope/limits and the 02 9833 4155 number still to verify. Not evidence of a Dubbo route.

evidence.claim: EcoCycle lists sites including Rocherlea (Tas), Kwinana (WA) and Auckland (NZ); its Campbellfield battery sorting and BIDS hub is at 5–11 Reo Crescent.
evidence.notes: Reo Crescent address from EcoBatt site page cited by the companion report.

evidence.claim: Dubbo Regional LGA population is about 57,400 (ABS ERP series).
evidence.notes: Secondary aggregator of ABS data.

evidence.claim: Australia generates roughly 23 kg of e-waste per person per year (Global E-waste Monitor 2019 as cited by Officeworks).
evidence.notes: National average, all electrical equipment by weight — not a Dubbo device count.

evidence.claim: EcoCycle/EcoBatt's visible Dubbo footprint is retail battery and phone bins, not general computer collection.
evidence.notes: Bin programmes accept batteries, phones and wearables; Bunnings excludes embedded-battery products. Store-by-store Dubbo bins not checked.

evidence.claim: Phones placed in Woolworths/BIG W units are on a recycling and data-destruction pathway; diverting them to reuse would conflict with depositors' expectations and the programme's stated purpose.
evidence.notes: Legal title transfer at deposit not established.

evidence.claim: EcoBatt and ecoe-waste are registered business names of ECOCYCLE PTY LTD (ABN 76 146 190 516), not necessarily separate legal subsidiaries.
evidence.notes: ABR record cited by the companion report.

evidence.claim: A WA regulator decision (Oct 2025) records EcoCycle's WA site routing embedded-battery products, including laptops, tablets and phones, to the Campbellfield BIDS plant.
evidence.notes: WA route only; not evidence of the NSW/Dubbo route.

evidence.claim: Council's adopted Waste Strategy records the Matthews Metals e-waste contract as 30 June 2023 to 30 June 2025, and names separate CRC battery contractors.
evidence.notes: Consistent with prior repo research (E31).

evidence.claim: Harvey Norman offers e-waste through Ecycle Solutions at participating stores.
evidence.notes: Dubbo participation unconfirmed.

evidence.claim: Queensland announced a $10 million grant for an EcoBatt all-chemistries battery plant at Hemmant on 26 November 2026.
evidence.notes: Planned infrastructure; not a Dubbo route.
